title: This Free Tool Can Reverse Engineer Any App
sources: GitHub, morluto/rea (README, checked 2026-11-17): 464,858 stars, created 2026-04-14, MIT; 'It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence'; setup 'npx rea-agents setup'; works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build; analysis runs locally; targets native binaries, Android APKs, websites, JS/Electron, .NET, Unity/Godot, GGUF/safetensors

lines.text: Ever seen a feature in an app and wondered exactly how it works?
lines.caps: Ever seen a *feature | and wondered | how it *works?

lines.text: Well, a free tool just made that possible, and it's exploding on GitHub.
lines.caps: A *free tool | just made it *possible, | and it's *exploding | on *GitHub.

lines.text: It's called REA, short for Reverse Engineer Anything,
and it passed four hundred and sixty thousand stars in about seven months.
You plug it into your AI coding agent, like Claude Code, Codex or Cursor,
lines.caps: Plug it into | your AI *agent, | *Claude Code, | Codex or *Cursor,

lines.text: then ask how a feature works, and your agent inspects the app, even without its source code,
lines.caps: ask how a feature *works, | your agent *inspects it, | even without | the *source code,

lines.text: right down to the binary level, and shows you the evidence.
lines.caps: down to the *binary level, | and shows the *evidence.

lines.text: It reads desktop apps, Android apps, websites, game files, and even AI model files,
all running locally, with one command to set it up.
lines.caps: all running *locally, | *one command | to set it up.

lines.text: Just one rule: only use it on apps you own or have permission to analyze.
lines.caps: One *rule: | only apps you *own | or have *permission | to analyze.
